title: Running a back room that actually works
target: How to keep the warehouse in TCG Card Shop Simulator useful, given that the game counts its shelves separately and lets stock live there boxed as well as unpacked.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Enough warehouse shelves for what you are holding
An idea of what you are about to put on the shop floor

steps.do: Put shelving in the warehouse rather than moving shop shelves back there.
steps.because: the game keeps a warehouse shelf type of its own (WarehouseShelf)

steps.do: Keep the shop floor for what is for sale, and move the rest to the back.
steps.because: an object can be marked as belonging in the warehouse (m_PlaceObjectInWarehouseOnly)

steps.do: Leave bulk purchases boxed until you need them.
steps.because: a stored thing keeps a boxed state of its own (isBoxed)

steps.do: Tidy the back room once, then leave it, instead of reshuffling it daily.
steps.because: each stored shelf is saved with its position and its contents (WarehouseShelfSaveData)

steps.do: Watch where the game will let a shelf go before you plan a big rearrangement.
steps.because: the game shows the area a shelf may legally be moved in (ShelfMoveStateValidArea)

commonMistakes: Dragging shop shelving into the warehouse instead of using warehouse shelves.
Unpacking everything on arrival and running out of display space.
Rearranging the back room in the middle of a busy trading day.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
